effect: Higher blood glucose led to insulin entering the blood; the route points toward muscle.
reaction: The connection between the message and its destination is clear.

choice.with: Muscle fibres beside a blood vessel

expectation: Insulin should help the muscle take in glucose and store some of it.

effect: Insulin helped muscle take in glucose and store it as carbohydrate, while remaining outside the cells.
reaction: It is useful to see that the message itself does not become part of the store.
reason: The pancreatic cell picture links the other hormone to lower blood glucose, matching the remaining goal.

effect: Lower blood glucose led to a hormone message that travels to the liver and helps break down its carbohydrate store.
reaction: The label makes the hormone's destination and purpose clear.
reason: The hormone is a message to release glucose, and the liver store contains linked glucose.

effect: The liver store released glucose into the blood, completing the between-meals route; the release signal eases as blood glucose rises.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the stored material become separate glucose again.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using insulin with muscle was worthwhile because it showed glucose becoming a store while insulin stayed outside as a message, not building material.

leastWorthwhile.text: Releasing the second hormone repeated the first hormone-release pattern, though it established the different condition and destination.

surprise.text: I was surprised that insulin stayed outside the muscle cells while helping them store glucose.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the pictures and goals connected each blood-glucose condition to a message and destination.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how the body uses these stores later, though this chapter's pairings were quite predictable.
